# MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo - ComfyUI Built-in Node Documentation

MiniMax H3 Reference to Video creates the text conditioning and the empty audio-video latent needed for MiniMax H3 reference-to-video generation.

MiniMax H3 Reference to Video creates the text conditioning and the empty audio-video latent needed for MiniMax H3 reference-to-video generation. You provide a prompt plus optional reference images, videos, and audio clips, and the node encodes these references into conditioning the model can use while generating. The prompt refers to the references with ` `, ` `, and ` ` tags.

Inputs

| Parameter | Description | Data Type | Required | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | CLIP model used to tokenize the prompt and encode the reference media into conditioning tokens. | CLIP | Yes | |
| `vae` | Video VAE. Without it reference images/videos only condition the text encoder. | VAE | No | |
| `audio_vae` | Audio VAE. Without it reference audio only conditions the text encoder. | VAE | No | |
| `prompt` | Text prompt for the video. Reference media can be addressed with ` `, ` `, and ` ` tags (1-based per type). Supports multiline and dynamic prompts. | STRING | Yes | |
| `width` | Width of the generated video in pixels (default: 1344). | INT | Yes | 32 to 16384 (step 32) |
| `height` | Height of the generated video in pixels (default: 768). | INT | Yes | 32 to 16384 (step 32) |
| `length` | Frame count at 24 fps, (124 = ~5s, trained range is ~124-362) (default: 124). | INT | Yes | 5 to 3600 (step 17) |
| `ref_image_size` | Reference image sizing. `match` scales each ref (down only, keeping aspect) to the generation’s pixel area; `max` uses the reference pipeline’s 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity. Reference tokens ride through every sampling step, so `max` can be several times slower (default: `match`). | COMBO | Yes | `"match"` `"max"` |
| `ref_images` | Growable slot: connect up to 9 reference images (`ref_image_1` … `ref_image_9`). Reference image (downscaled to 2048 short edge if larger, never upscaled). | IMAGE | No | 0 to 9 |
| `ref_videos` | Growable slot: connect up to 3 reference videos (`ref_video_1` … `ref_video_3`). Reference video frames at 24 fps (2-15s). | IMAGE | No | 0 to 3 |
| `ref_video_audios` | Growable slot: connect up to 3 soundtracks (`ref_video_audio_1` … `ref_video_audio_3`). Soundtrack of the same-numbered reference video. | AUDIO | No | 0 to 3 |
| `ref_audios` | Growable slot: connect up to 3 standalone reference audio clips (`ref_audio_1` … `ref_audio_3`). Standalone reference audio. | AUDIO | No | 0 to 3 |

Notes:

- The prompt refers to reference media with 1-based tags per type: ` ` for images, ` ` for videos, and ` ` for audio. References are presented to the model in a fixed order: images, then videos (with each soundtrack’s ` ` label right before its ` `), then standalone audio.
- A soundtrack connected to `ref_video_audio_N` is used with the reference video connected to `ref_video_N`.
- Reference videos must contain at least 5 frames (~0.2 seconds at 24 fps), otherwise the node raises an error. Frames beyond the requested `length` are trimmed, and the remaining frame count is adjusted to a value supported by the model.
- The requested `length` is aligned to a supported frame count before the latent is created.
- Without `vae`, reference images and videos only condition the text encoder (no reference latents are produced). Without `audio_vae`, reference audio only conditions the text encoder.

Outputs

| Output Name | Description | Data Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `positive` | Conditioning containing the encoded prompt. When reference media and the relevant VAEs are provided, it also contains the encoded reference image, video, and audio content used by the MiniMax H3 model. | CONDITIONING |
| `latent` | Empty audio-video latent at the requested `width`, `height`, and `length` (frame count), including the aligned video latent and audio latent. | LATENT |

Key features

- Native stereo audio: Dialogue, SFX, and music in one MP4
- Multimodal context: Combine text, image, video, and audio references
- Reference-driven generation: Lock identity, style, motion, camera, or voice from references
- Instruction following: Describe reference-to-shot relationships in natural language
- Accurate text rendering: Clean spelled-out text and brand elements
- Open weights: Full local control in ComfyUI

...

## Text to Video (T2V)

Generate videos from an input image, with optional first/last-frame control

## Reference to Video (R2V)

Lock in a character, style, motion, camera move, or voice from reference images, videos, and audio

## Multiframe Reference

Anchor reference frames at specific points along the output timeline with chained Add Guide nodes

## Fun ControlNet Union

Drive H3 with a Canny, Depth, HED, MLSD, or Pose control video, or run video inpainting with a mask

MiniMax H3 Image to Video covers T2V and first/last-frame I2V (`t2va` / `fl2va`). MiniMax H3 Reference to Video covers R2V (`ref2va`).

Reference conditioning only applies when it reaches the sampler. T2V/I2V templates sample inside a subgraph wired to Image to Video only. A Reference to Video node on the canvas is ignored without error. Use the R2V template (or a workflow built from it) for reference-driven output.

highlights:
## MiniMax H3 ref2va - Lip Sync + TURBO MiniMax H3 Ref2VA v1.0

### MiniMax H3 Ref2VA — Audio-Driven Turbo (Image + Audio to Video)

A ComfyUI workflow for MiniMax H3 that drives generation with your own reference audio instead of relying on the model's own invented sound. Built on H3's ref2va (reference-to-video/audio) task — the only H3 task type whose node exposes an audio-reference input — so a real audio file (dialogue for lip-sync, an SFX cue like a splash, ambience, etc.) can be handed to the model alongside a reference image and threaded into the generated clip's timing.

Built entirely from stock ComfyUI core nodes — no custom node packs required.

What it does

- Takes a reference image and a reference audio clip, plus a text prompt, and generates a video conditioned on both via `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo`.

- Auto-appends a fixed audio-retention instruction to your prompt `: fully_copy — is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track`) via a `StringConcatenate` node, so the model is always told to preserve your audio as the literal final track rather than treating it as a loose style cue — you don't have to remember to type this yourself.

- Turbo LoRA switcher: pick any turbo LoRA from a dropdown, and a `StringContains`-based logic chain reads the filename for `"8step"` or `"4step"` and automatically sets the matching step count — so the step count can't silently drift out of sync with whichever LoRA file you actually selected.

- TURBO toggle: flip it off to bypass the LoRA switch entirely and fall back to the full ~20-step base ref2va model, regardless of which LoRA is selected in the dropdown.

- Everything (model loading, CLIP/VAE loading, sampling, turbo logic) is packed into one collapsed subgraph with a small set of exposed widgets, so the graph stays readable at a glance instead of a wall of wired nodes.

Requirements

- ComfyUI with core MiniMax H3 support `comfy-core`) — no custom node packs 

- `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` (diffusion model)

- `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` (text encoder)

- `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors` + `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors` (VAEs)

- Optional: one or more MiniMax H3 turbo LoRAs (filename must contain `4step` or `8step` for the auto-switcher to detect it — anything else falls back to 20-step base behavior even with TURBO on)

Usage

1. Load the workflow into ComfyUI.

2. In Load Image, upload your reference/subject image.

3. In Load Audio (splash SFX reference), upload your reference audio clip.

4. Set your Resolution Selector aspect ratio and megapixels.

5. Write your scene prompt describing the shot(s) and timeline — reference your inputs as ` ` and ` ` in the text (see the pinned note node for the subject/retention tag format this workflow expects).

6. Pick a turbo LoRA from the dropdown (or leave TURBO off to skip it) and set Duration/Frame Rate as usual.

7. Queue the prompt.

Notes / tuning

- If your output looks undercooked or noisy at low step counts, check the console for `lora key not loaded` warnings — that confirms whether the selected turbo LoRA actually applied its weights rather than silently mismatching against the ref2va checkpoint.

- The audio-retention instruction is appended automatically; if you want H3 to treat your reference audio more loosely (e.g. as a rhythm/atmosphere cue rather than a literal final track), edit or remove the Audio Guidance primitive string node rather than fighting it in your own prompt text.

- TURBO off is the safest fallback if a LoRA misbehaves or you're troubleshooting quality — it forces the full base step count independent of whatever's in the LoRA dropdown.

- This is ref2va, not fl2va: there's no `first_framelast_frame` keyframe conditioning here, only reference image(s) + reference audio. If you need locked start/end frames, that's a different H3 task type.

- H3 generations are capped at roughly 15s natively (17-frame-per-block grid at 24fps) — this workflow doesn't chain multiple generations for longer output.

# MiniMax H3: Reference to Video

Generate a new video by feeding MiniMax H3 a reference image, up to nine images, three videos, and three audio clips alongside a text prompt, letting the model match character identity, motion, camera, voice, or style from those sources while producing native stereo audio in a single pass. Output is a single MP4 video at up to 2K resolution and 24fps for roughly 15 seconds. Ideal for character-consistent animation, style-transfer video generation, and audio-synced content creation.

...

This workflow demonstrates MiniMax H3’s reference-to-video generation in ComfyUI: you provide a text prompt plus up to nine reference images, three short reference videos, and three audio clips, and the model produces a single MP4 with native stereo audio in one pass. The MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo node is the core, fusing multi-modal context (identity, motion, camera, style, and voice) with your prompt to synthesize a ~15s clip at up to 2K resolution and 24fps.

Under the hood, the Switch Model and Settings group loads the MiniMax H3 model stack via UNETLoader and CLIPLoader, while KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, SamplerCustomAdvanced, and BasicGuider manage sampling behavior (seeded by RandomNoise for reproducibility). ResolutionSelector sets a 16:9 size aligned to multiples of 32, and ComfyMathExpression with PrimitiveFloat handles derived values like frame count from duration and fps. After generation, VAELoader provides both video and audio VAEs; VAEDecode reconstructs frames from video latents and VAEDecodeAudio reconstructs stereo waveforms. highlights:
Version: 1.0.0 Date: September 2026 Key Nodes: `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo`, `LoadAudio`, `MiniMaxH3RefModsLoader`, `MiniMaxH3RefModApply`, `MiniMaxH3MotionContext`, `MiniMaxH3MotionContextTrim`

## 1. Overview & Capability 

MiniMax-H3 natively supports multimodal reference audio conditioning via the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. By feeding an audio track (WAV/MP3) into `ref_audios.ref_audio_0`, MiniMax-H3 encodes the waveform into its 40Hz joint video-audio latent space, achieving:

1. High-Precision Lip Synchronization: Characters articulate exact phonemes and song lyrics in sync with vocals.
2. Synchronized Performance & Emote Acting: Micro-gestures, breathing, and eye movements follow the cadence and dynamic volume of the audio.
3. 1:1 Audio Track Reuse: The generated video reproduces the clean source audio without speech degradation or acoustic distortion.

## 2. Audio-Conditioned Node Architecture 

```
[ LoadAudio (audio.wav) ] ──────> [ ref_audios.ref_audio_0 ]
                                         │
[ CLIPLoader (Qwen3-VL) ] ──────> [ clip ] ──> [ MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo ] ──> [ conditioning ] ──> [ MiniMaxH3RefModApply ]
[ VAELoader (Audio VAE) ] ──────> [ audio_vae ]                                            ▲
[ VAELoader (Video VAE) ] ──────> [ vae ]                                                  │
                                                                                [ MiniMaxH3RefModsLoader ]

```

### Graph Connection Details: 

- `LoadAudio`: Loads the local audio file from ComfyUI's `input/` folder.
- `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo`:

- `ref_audios.ref_audio_0`: Connects to `LoadAudio` output.
- `audio_vae`: Connects to `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors`.
- `vae`: Connects to `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors`.
- `clip`: Connects to Qwen-VL clip loader (or Power Lora loader).
- `MiniMaxH3RefModsLoader` + `MiniMaxH3RefModApply`: Injects character reference latent adapters directly into the conditioned text stream without interfering with the audio latent.

...

## 6. Silent Reaction & Coverage Shots: Node Disconnection Protocol 

When generating non-singing, silent reaction shots, listening coverage, or ambient cutaways to intercut into a scene:

- Never leave the `LoadAudio` / `ref_audios` node connected while instructing the character to be silent in the text prompt.
- Active audio latent conditioning causes MiniMax-H3's cross-attention to automatically animate mouth movements and phoneme articulation, overriding negative text instructions like `"No dialogue"` or `"Lips sealed"`.
- The Rule: Physically disconnect the audio reference node for all listening, reaction, or breathing takes. Only wire the audio input when the on-screen character is actively articulating vocals.

highlights:
### Let's clarify the premise first.

Currently, it is not yet possible to make MiniMax H3 itself speak clear Japanese. What this article introduces is a method to "match the mouth movements of the generated video to the timing of audio prepared externally."

The audio actually released is not the audio generated by H3 itself. I remove the audio from the video generated by H3 and overlay the audio of the same lines used for reference (AivisSpeech) during video editing. Please read on with the understanding that the "process of creating mouth movements" and the "process of creating voices" are still separate things.

...

## Core Discovery: Passing audio to `ref_audios` syncs the mouth

MiniMax H3 has a node called `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` (Ref2VA), where you can pass audio as a "reference." When you pass the dialogue audio created in advance with AivisSpeech to this `ref_audios`, I found that H3 generates a video where the character's mouth moves in sync with that speech timing . There is no need for manual post-production lip-sync correction, such as fixing mouth shapes frame by frame.

However, the speech quality generated by H3 itself is not something that can be used as is. In actual production, I remove only the audio from the video produced by H3 and overlay the audio of the same lines used for reference (AivisSpeech) during video editing. In other words, "the mouth syncs" here means that the mouth movements on the video side match the timing of the audio. It is accurate to understand that the audio itself is not an H3 generation, but something recorded separately and matched later. 

### There is a trap in how to pass it

I spent a lot of time on this, but if you get one part of the delivery method wrong, it will be silently ignored without even throwing an error.

```
✕ {"ref_audios": {"ref_audio_0": ["1101", 0]}}   # 入れ子にすると無視される
○ {"ref_audios.ref_audio_0": ["1101", 0]}        # ドットで繋いだ、この形だけが正しい
```

Audio is loaded with the `LoadAudio` node and indicated in the prompt as ` `. You can pass up to three files. 

### Do not write the dialogue text

There is a dialogue text format like ` [Japanese]…… `, but if you are passing reference audio, do not write this. Since the audio side provides both the content and the timing, passing both at the same time will cause it to speak twice. I actually had an example where words were doubled, like "Nice to meet you, I am Alto for Alto."

...

## Controlled experiment: Is it really working?

Since "no error = working" is not always true, I compared it by changing only the presence or absence of reference audio while keeping the seed and prompt the same.

 With Reference Audio Without Reference Audio Speech Start 0.3073 sec 0.2505 sec Breath Start 1.2460 sec 1.0571 sec Waveform Correlation +0.732 +0.013

Only when reference audio is provided do the speech start and breath timings approach the actual audio, and the waveform correlation changes significantly. Without reference audio, H3 is just moving its mouth "plausibly" without knowing the content of the audio, so the correlation is near zero.

### Match the clip duration with the reference audio duration

If the clip (video duration) is longer than the reference audio, H3 will repeat the end of the sentence to fill the remaining time.

In actual measurements, in a case where the clip was 3.75 seconds against a 3.323-second reference, it spoke for an extra 0.43 seconds (H3's speech ended at 3.41 seconds, while the reference was 2.97 seconds. The difference is exactly 0.43 seconds). Therefore, you need to pad the beginning and end of the reference audio with silence to match the clip duration exactly.

### You cannot create "pauses" with prompts. Use silence in the audio

This was the most surprising point this time. Even if you write "remain silent and still for the first second" in the prompt, H3 barely follows it. In actual measurements, it deviated by 0.9 to 2.1 seconds.

On the other hand, if you create a silent section at the very beginning of the reference audio itself, H3 follows it with surprising accuracy.

Boundary Time of Provided Audio H3 Output Difference Start of Speech 0.919 sec 0.912 sec 0.007 sec Breath Start 1.862 sec 1.858 sec 0.004 sec Breath End 2.389 sec 2.383 sec 0.006 sec End of Speech 3.574 sec 3.571 sec 0.003 sec

The conclusion is that timing control is done through silence in the audio file itself, not through words in the prompt.

## Biggest discovery: The "0.9-second lead silence" rule

This was the most practical discovery in this verification.

If there is 0.9 seconds or more of silence (lead silence) from the beginning of the cut until the voice actually starts, the lip-sync will match; if it is less than 0.5 seconds, it will always fail. H3 seems unable to grasp the timing of speech when provided with audio that starts speaking immediately.

Here are the actual measurements where only the conditions were changed with the same seed and same reference configuration.

Cut Lead Silence Waveform Correlation Result A (Old) 1.919 sec +0.989 ✅ A (New) 1.919 sec +0.930 ✅ C (Old) 0.935 sec +0.702 ✅ B (Old) 0.767 sec +0.097 ❌ C (New) 0.454 sec +0.366 ❌ B (New) 0.058 sec +0.120 ❌

Lead silence is calculated using the following formula. You must also include the silence at the beginning contained within the dialogue itself in the calculation.

```
リード無音 ＝（台詞の開始時刻＋その台詞自身の頭の無音）－ カットの開始時刻
```

...

## Summary: Recipe for syncing lips to external audio

Note: "Lip-sync" here means that the mouth movements on the video side match the timing of the audio. The audio generated by H3 itself is not yet of practical quality, and the audio actually released is recorded separately (AivisSpeech) and overlaid later during video editing. 

1. Match the length of the reference audio (lines created with AivisSpeech, etc.) exactly to the length of the clip
2. Insert at least 0.9 seconds of silent lead-in before the lines (less than 0.5 seconds will likely fail)
3. When you want to create a "pause," do it with silence on the audio side, not with prompts
4. If there are two or more speakers, provide a combination of overall audio + individual speaker audio (using only individual speaker audio will cause it to break down). This completely eliminates the mix-up where "one person keeps talking until the other person's lines" (measured 12/12). 
5. Pass `ref_audios` using dot notation (`ref_audios.ref_audio_0`). If you nest them, they will be silently ignored.
6. Do not easily discard verification metrics like waveform correlation, even if they are inconvenient.

I hope this is helpful for those who are generating videos locally and are struggling with "mouth movements not matching."

highlights:
## What is MiniMax H3 Reference-to-Video?

MiniMax H3 (known commercially as Hailuo 3.0) is an open-weights, omni-modal diffusion transformer that generates video and native stereo audio simultaneously. While the MiniMax H3 image-to-video (`fl2va`) model locks onto an opening or closing keyframe, the Reference-to-Video (`ref2va`) model injects encoded reference tokens into every denoising step so you can direct new scenes while preserving identity, style, motion, or voice.

Using the built-in `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node, the same workflow handles four core tasks:

- Multi-image character and style consistency: Feed up to 9 reference images (` ` to ` `) to keep character faces, outfits, props, and environments consistent across multi-shot camera cuts.
- Character replacement and motion transfer: Connect a reference video-to-video clip (` `) alongside character photos to swap the actor while keeping the original camera movement, lighting, and choreography.
- Zero-shot voice cloning and lip-sync: Pass a reference audio clip (` `) either to clone a speaker’s vocal timbre for newly written dialogue or to copy a voiceover or song track so the character lip-syncs to the exact waveform.
- Joint stereo sound design: Generate spoken lines, physical Foley, ambient room tone, and background music aligned frame-by-frame with the visual action.

...

### Step 4: Upload the reference images (or video and audio)

In the User Inputs group, upload your reference images to the two Load Image nodes:

- The left Load Image node (`#137`) connects to `ref_image_0` on MiniMax H3 Reference to Video, which corresponds to ` ` in your prompt.
- The right Load Image node (`#139`) connects to `ref_image_1`, which corresponds to ` ` in your prompt.

You can download and use these two 16:9 test images to reproduce the cyber-ronin and mechanical kitsune demo:

Reference Image 1 (`ref_image_0` / ` `): Cyber-ronin character (` `).

Reference Image 2 (`ref_image_1` / ` `): Mechanical kitsune guardian (` `).

Notice that the MiniMax H3 Reference to Video node automatically spawns a new empty slot (`ref_image_2`, up to `ref_image_8`) each time you connect an image.

How to connect a reference video or voice clip (optional):

- Reference video (` `): Do not drag a standard Load Video node’s `VIDEO` output directly to `ref_video_0`, because `ref_video_0` expects decoded `IMAGE` frames. Instead, connect Load Video to the built-in Get Video Components node, then wire `images` to `ref_video_0` (and optionally `audio` to `ref_video_audio_0`).
- Standalone reference audio (` `): Add a built-in Load Audio node and connect its `AUDIO` output to `ref_audio_0` for voice cloning or lip-sync.

...

### Step 6: Revise the prompt

The full demo prompt is already loaded inside the Input Text (Prompt) node (`#138`). When writing your own reference-to-video prompt, follow these structure rules and tips:

- Declare your reference tags up front: Open with a look and style header (`Live-action cinematic sci-fi fantasy film look...`) and state which connected tags to use (`Use and as character references`). Tags are numbered 1-based per modality in the order they are connected.
- Direct timecoded shots with visual anchors: Start each cut on a new line with a timestamp (`[Shot 1] At 00:00.000...`, `[Shot 2] At 00:02.500...`). Always repeat 2 to 3
